Peak El Niño insurance strategy

Point-in-time technical and short-pressure simulation for the 12 screenshot tickers. Orders execute after the signal date, and ATR stops use only prior information.

Massive daily prices, short interest, short volume, NBBO quotes and point-in-time share counts · Initial capital $100,000 · Price returns exclude dividends

Result. The enhanced strategy ended at $78,082, a -21.9% cumulative return across the three non-contiguous tradable windows. Core MA/ATR returned -24.7% and passive screenshot-basket exposure returned 481.4%. These are small-event historical results, not evidence that insurance payouts caused the moves.
2.0× ATRtrailing stop
LMND 24.5%best enhanced ticker
ALL -44.0%worst enhanced ticker
Alternative-data limit. Massive short interest begins in December 2017 and daily short volume in February 2024. Those fields cannot be backfilled into 2009–10 or 2015–16. The historical quote input is a single top-of-book NBBO snapshot per week, not a full depth-of-book reconstruction. The 2026-03 to 2026-07 peak first becomes tradable under the timing rule in June 2026; it is therefore not backtested.

Key findings

  • The enhanced overlay did not improve profit. It returned -21.92% with a -26.32% maximum drawdown. Core MA/ATR returned -24.75% with a -30.12% drawdown. The extra confirmation reduced risk modestly but cut return sharply.
  • Passive exposure dominated in these hand-picked bullish windows. The screenshot basket gained 481.4%, but suffered a -38.0% drawdown. Much of the 2023–24 gain came from highly volatile newer listings, particularly ROOT.
  • BAP is the main enhanced-strategy winner. Its compounded enhanced return was 24.5%. BAP is Credicorp, a diversified financial group with an insurance subsidiary, so this cannot be interpreted as a clean catastrophe-insurer payout effect.
  • Short/order-book confirmation was weak directionally. The enhanced portfolio's active-day hit rate was 48.4%, below a neutral 50% benchmark. BAP and HIG were the most useful confirmations; PGR, KNSL, LMND and ROOT detracted.
  • The 2023–24 enhanced overlay returned only 1.00%. The price-only core returned 8.69% in the same trade window. Short volume was available only from February 2024, so it influenced less than four months of that episode.

Why the passive basket can work

The passive basket benefits when the event window contains a broad insurance-sector or risk-on repricing: an equal-dollar allocation spreads company-specific risk, keeps exposure through short-lived signal reversals, and lets winners compound without discretionary exits. It also avoids the enhanced strategy's frequent signal changes and ATR-stop losses. This is a mechanism consistent with the results, not proof that El Niño caused the returns.

Against the US P&C insurance benchmark (KIE proxy), the basket tests whether the predefined company basket added value beyond broad insurance-sector exposure. KIE is an ETF proxy, not a pure index or a claim-loss index; the comparison therefore measures investable sector performance rather than underwriting profitability.

Returns include 0.07% transaction cost per side at entry and exit and a 20% tax on positive realized event gains. The model does not include dividends, which makes this a conservative comparison for dividend-paying insurers.

The timeline connects only the tested windows. Capital sits in cash between them; the chart removes those blank calendar gaps.

Actual severe months are shifted three months to form tradable windows: December 2009–January 2010 becomes March–April 2010; August 2015–March 2016 becomes November 2015–June 2016; September 2023–February 2024 becomes December 2023–May 2024.

Rules fixed before testing

  1. Peak regime: ONI ≥ +1.5°C. A three-month delay converts the revised centered ONI observation into an available-information trading flag.
  2. Trend: +1 when Close > SMA20 > SMA60 and five-day momentum is positive; −1 for the reverse; otherwise zero.
  3. Volatility filter: trade only when ATR10 / Close exceeds its trailing 60-session median.
  4. Order book: weekly NBBO imbalance I=(bid size−ask size)/(bid size+ask size). +1 when I>0.10, −1 when I<−0.10. The snapshot is the final quote strictly before 16:00 New York time and becomes usable next session.
  5. Short interest: settlement observations are delayed ten calendar days. A decline greater than 5% scores +1; an increase greater than 5% scores −1.
  6. Short volume: the five-session short-volume ratio is compared with its trailing 20-session median. A difference beyond ±3 percentage points supplies a weak directional confirmation.
  7. Composite: Score=(0.55T+0.20B+0.15SI+0.10SV)/available weights. Trend must be nonzero, agree with the composite, and produce an aligned score of at least 0.55.
  8. Execution and risk: next-session open; 2.5× Wilder ATR(10) trailing stop; 7.5 bp per transaction side; 3% annualized short-borrow charge; equal weight across eligible tickers; maximum gross exposure 100%.

What the result does and does not show

  • The strategy monetizes directional volatility during an ENSO-conditioned window. It does not observe company claim payments, catastrophe reserves, insured-loss announcements or premium repricing directly.
  • Short volume includes liquidity provision and hedging. It is not a daily change in short interest and is not automatically bearish.
  • Top-of-book imbalance is noisy and can change immediately. A weekly closing snapshot is a coarse directional measure, not an executable historical order book.
  • High volatility makes an ATR stop wider in dollars. The 2.5× multiple was fixed, not selected from the winning test result.
  • Dividends are excluded. This understates long total returns and overstates short returns. Borrow availability, recalls, locate fees, taxes and market impact are not modeled.
  • Only three completed tradable windows exist, and newer listings participate in one. Results are highly vulnerable to event selection, ticker survivorship and one-company news.

Metric formulas

TR_t=max(H_t−L_t, |H_t−C_(t−1)|, |L_t−C_(t−1)|); ATR10 is Wilder's exponentially smoothed ten-session true range.

Strategy return compounds marked-to-market daily returns after transaction and modeled borrow costs. Ending capital=100,000×∏(1+r_t).

Maximum drawdown=min_t(W_t/max_(s≤t)W_s−1). Sharpe=mean(r)/sd(r)×√252, with no risk-free-rate subtraction.

Exposure=mean(|position|). For the portfolio, this is the mean invested fraction across eligible names.

Files and sources

Market data use Massive's daily aggregates, short-interest, short-volume, historical ticker-reference and quote endpoints. ONI comes from the supplied monthly dataset; operational definitions are available from NOAA CPC.

Prepared 13 September 2026. Historical research only, not investment advice.
